name: Is design-build cheaper than hiring an architect and contractor separately?

mainEntity.name: Is design-build cheaper than hiring an architect and contractor separately?
mainEntity.text: Is design-build cheaper than hiring an architect and contractor separately?

acceptedAnswer.text: Design-build is often more cost-efficient over the life of a project because design and construction are coordinated from the start. That can reduce rework, change orders, and schedule delays, especially on complex Los Angeles remodels or custom homes. However, it is not automatically the lowest sticker price. A separate architect-and-contractor setup may appear cheaper at first if design is developed without construction input, but it can become more expensive when plans exceed budget or need to be revised for permitting or buildability. For homeowners, the real question is total value: speed, fewer surprises, and better alignment between design intent and construction budget. Ask each firm how often they revisit costs during design, how many rounds of revisions are included, and whether the team is incentivized to keep the project on budget. The cheapest quote is not necessarily the least expensive project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design-build is not always cheaper upfront, but it can lower total project cost by reducing redesign, delays, and coordination mistakes. Separate architect-and-contractor delivery can look less expensive early on, but it often creates more change orders and longer schedules if the budget is not aligned during design.
